Source (%1$d Hz) → Oboe Exclusive bypasses Android Mixer. Non-USB direct write, not labeled Bit-Perfect.
AAudio Shared · System Mixer In Path

In Shared mode AudioFlinger forces all audio streams to resample to device native rate. Even if the app layer does not resample, the system mixer still performs SRC internally.\n\nSuggestion: switch to Oboe Exclusive mode for true bit-perfect output.
Audio is being resampled from source rate to device native rate. Resampling happens in the Oboe/AAudio layer as software SRC, does not affect quality.

• Live Monitor — polls getSharingMode() every second, detects system preemption/downgrade
• AF Track Flags — AudioFlinger low-level track flags (0x000=Shared, 0x100=MMAP, 0x004=Direct)
• Focus Events — audio focus change log, shows system audio preemption timeline
• Bit-Perfect only holds under USB DAC Exclusive direct write: bypasses AudioFlinger and Mixer
• Under AAudio Shared mode AudioFlinger always participates, internal resampling uncontrollable

Template takes over the transition — the classic effect and depth below are bypassed for this section
djay Crossfader FX — Filter (reverse sweep: A HPF up / B LPF down), Echo, Brake Drop, Dissolve (reverb). Pick one to take over the transition; the classic effect & depth stand down.
Change speed while holding pitch. Off = classic pitch bend (speed and pitch move together)
Auto-transpose outgoing track to harmonize with the incoming key
Which effect to apply to the routed stem. Auto derives it from the DJ transition template; the other options lock it (e.g. LPF mutes that stem\'s highs, Stem gain makes it stand out).
Applies the FX to that one stem instead of the whole track — Drums + Filter keeps the old vocal clear while the new drums come in. Needs a cached track: the first play of a song has no stems yet
Tempo Blend keeps both tracks at natural pitch & speed, so stem routing is not applied.
Loops the outgoing track in 1/2 or 1/4-beat slices with a chopped gate — the Hip-Hop / Trap transition staple
Stretches the incoming track to the current tempo — beats line up, pitch stays put
Off — BPM differences stay audible as drift
Time-stretch kicks in only during a crossfade and only when both tracks have a known BPM. Differences beyond the limit are left alone rather than stretched into mush.
